content_of_post_to_comment:
I’m not sure if this is the right forum to post this on, but I just need some advice or reassurance or something.

I am 18F in my first semester of college. I go to a smaller liberal arts school that I actually really like, but unfortunately everywhere I go I am forced to bring myself along too.

I was doing pretty well the first few weeks, but then what usually happens eventually is now happening. No surprises.

For context, I was diagnosed with anxiety and depression when I was around 12, so this isn’t new. The depression became clinical and debilitating in high school, so I got on medication, did inpatient treatment twice, and basically missed a whole semester of school because I was too anxious to go or even get off of the couch. I did about two months of outpatient treatment at the psych hospital for my severe depression during that time when I could. My point here is that this stuff isn’t new. It’s been years of this exact same stuff I just can’t seem to get over it.

Although I managed to get into a good university, I struggled in high school a lot with turning things in on time and just in general terrible executive dysfunction and time management. For the most part, it all got done, but it was after it was already a week overdue and beat myself up over my lack of ability to focus and just get the work done.

Same thing is happening to me now in college. It wasn’t like I didn’t expect this, I just figured hm maybe a new environment and situation will help me. But I am the person I’ve always been, and location and circumstance did not and won’t change that.

I genuinely don’t know what’s wrong with me. It’s this weird feeling where I know something is wrong with me, and everyone else knows something is wrong with me, but we all just ignore and I struggle. I blame it all on my depression and anxiety, because that is a huge part of it, and while medication does help me to be able to function everyday as human being, it falls short in discipline.

Although I turn in late work all the time, it is almost always good. I get A’s on my papers. I take my time to write them and genuinely care about what I am studying because I would genuinely rather turn in a good assignment late than turn in a half-assed one that doesn’t represent my abilities on time. I keep high standards for myself which also contributes to some of this.

What happens a lot is that I’ll get close to finishing an assignment, but then I won’t submit it because it’s like not good enough or something. I had a paper due that I just turned in almost two weeks late because although I had every paragraph written for the most part, I hadn’t read over it, or did the bibliography, and a few other things and I couldn’t get myself to turn it on.

The paper itself was probably good, but unfortunately I’ll probably receive a bad grade just cause of how late it was.

I’m getting long winded, so I’ll try to wrap this up. I reached out to my schools mental fitness center and requested an academic coach, but I have yet to receive an email back about that. I just went back to the page to schedule a counseling session with one of the on-campus counselors but they have no availability that works with my class schedule. I’ve tried therapy anyway, with probably about six different therapists, but I never really found it to help at all, and even if wanted to go back to chat with my old therapist I can’t because she’s not licensed in the state my school is in. I know exactly what I should do to combat these things and cope, there’s just something blocking me. It might ignorance or laziness or maybe I just don’t want it bad enough. But I do. I really really want it.

I’m not sure where discipline meets depression, but it seems that line is blurred for me.

I’ll have faith sometimes that I can do better, but then I’ll get an automated email that I missed an assignment I totally forgot about and then it sends me back into a spiral again. This stuff may seem minor, but it genuinely makes me want to die and give up and it causes me to think impulsive thoughts.

I really don’t ever want to get out of bed. I don’t want to do things. I hate being awake so I kind of sleep a lot.

Often, very often, I consider that I might have ADHD. My brother has it and my mom too. But I don’t know where the symptoms of depression and anxiety end and ADHD starts. Medication for my diagnoses have genuinely saved my life, and I’m wondering is that could be the same if I ever got on stimulants. I don’t know.

I feel so lazy every time I think about this stuff because what the hell why can’t I just do the work on time? Why can’t I just get out of bed? Why do such simple interactions bring about this anxiety? It all just makes me so so depressed.

My missing assignments in one of my courses is reaching double digits. And I’ll get it done, it will just take me a minute.

I guess I want to know if anyone can relate? I’m drowning in my habits and these thoughts. I’m feeling hopeless and impulsive.
